title: Titanium TAVI Frame
alloyReason: Nitinol (ASTM F2063, 55-60 wt% Ni) is specified for Titanium TAVI Frame where superelastic recovery up to 8% strain at body temperature enables self-expanding or self-centering functionality. The austenite finish temperature (A_f) is set 10-15°C below operating temperature to ensure complete martensite-to-austenite transformation. This shape memory behavior is uniquely suited for Transcatheter aortic valve replacement frame (Nitinol) requiring reversible deformation. This rationale is driven by transcatheter aortic valve replacement frame (nitinol) and service environment demands.
process: CNC swiss turning for cardiovascular geometry
Ultrasonic clean Class 10k with 0.5mm corner radius
surfaceTreatment: Electropolishing + passivation per ASTM F86 (20-30% HNO3, 30min @50C) achieving Ra <0.2um for implant-grade finish — tailored for transcatheter aortic valve application
commonFailures: Fe contamination from machining - requires acid passivation 20-30% HNO3, 30min @50C per ASTM F86 — critical for transcatheter aortic valve performance

faq.q: Is Titanium TAVI Frame MRI-safe or MRI-conditional?
faq.a: Nitinol is non-ferromagnetic (magnetic susceptibility 1.00005 × 10⁻⁶ cgs) and generates negligible MRI artifact compared to 316L stainless steel. Titanium TAVI Frame is classified as MR-Conditional under ASTM F2052/F2213 testing at 1.5T and 3.0T field strengths. Specific absorption rates remain within safe limits for transcatheter aortic valve configurations.

faq.q: What is the typical lead time for Titanium TAVI Frame orders?
faq.a: Standard lead time for Titanium TAVI Frame is 15-25 business days depending on quantity and complexity. Rush orders (3-5 working days) are available for prototype evaluation. Sample evaluation (1-5 units) can be expedited to 5-7 business days. Volume pricing is available for production quantities above 100 units.

faq.q: What material certifications are provided with Titanium TAVI Frame?
faq.a: Each Titanium TAVI Frame shipment includes EN 10204 Type 3.1 mill test certificate with chemical analysis, mechanical properties, and heat identification. Dimensional inspection reports and Certificate of Conformance (CoC) are standard. First Article Inspection Reports (FAIR) per AS9102 are available on request for transcatheter aortic valve.
